article.content: Four Apache Struts vulnerabilities described in security advisories could expose affected applications to remote code execution, denial of service, and cross-user data disclosure. The recommended fixes are Struts 7.4.0 or later, or Struts 6.12.0 or later for deployments remaining on the 6.x maintenance branch. The issues involve legacy action mapping, decimal rendering, REST request processing, and localized message formatting. Exposure depends on application configuration and feature usage, rather than the installed version alone. Apache Struts Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-104711, reported by LeaveSong and rated Moderate, allows crafted requests to inject OGNL expressions through the legacy RESTful action mapper, potentially resulting in remote code execution. Affected versions include Struts 2.0.0–2.3.37, 2.5.0–2.5.33, and 6.0.0–6.11.0. Struts 7.0.0–7.3.0 is affected only when its OGNL allowlist is disabled; the default configuration remains protected. Applications using the default mapper, restful2 mapper, or REST plugin are not affected by this particular vulnerability. Apache documents these as distinct mapping implementations, so identifying the configured mapper is essential during exposure assessment. CVE-2026-104712, reported by 0xCc.zhang and rated Moderate, affects applications that bind request parameters to java.math.BigDecimal properties and subsequently render those properties through the Struts tag library. A small request can generate a disproportionately large response, allowing unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server CPU and outbound network capacity through sustained low-volume traffic. Affected releases are Struts 2.5.14–2.5.33, 6.0.0–6.11.0, and 7.0.0–7.3.0. Other numeric types and responses generated by the JSON or REST plugins are unaffected. As a temporary workaround, developers can register a converter that bounds decimal scale before rendering. Application-wide converters belong in struts-conversion.properties at the classpath root; older deployments use xwork-conversion.properties. CVE-2026-104713, reported by n0mi1k and rated Important, concerns unbounded request-body reads in the optional REST plugin. A single oversized request can trigger proportional memory allocation, exhaust the Java heap, and disrupt other users. The issue affects Struts 2.1.8–2.3.37, 2.5.0–2.5.33, 6.0.0–6.11.0, and 7.0.0–7.3.0. Fixed releases introduce a default limit of 2,097,152 characters, configurable through struts.rest.content.maxLength. Oversized bodies are rejected before action invocation. Until patching, administrators should enforce request-body limits at the reverse proxy or servlet container. CVE-2026-104714, also reported by n0mi1k and rated Moderate, affects shared formatters used for localized messages containing date or time arguments. Concurrent requests can interfere, causing one user’s value to appear in another user’s response or triggering server errors. Ordinary traffic can expose the flaw without malicious input. The vulnerability spans Struts 2.0.0–2.3.37, 2.5.0–2.5.33, 6.0.0–6.11.0, and 7.0.0–7.3.0. Developers can temporarily preformat date and time values before message interpolation. Upgrading addresses all four issues; end-of-life branches require migration to supported releases. Join 16,000+ SOC teams using ANY.RUN to streamline threat investigations and reduce manual effort. slides.headlineRest: Vulnerabilities Expose Applications to RCE, DoS & Data Disclosure
slides.body: Four newly detailed vulnerabilities in Apache Struts could allow remote code execution, denial of service, and cross-user data disclosure in affected applications. These issues stem from legacy action mapping, decimal rendering, REST request processing, and localized message formatting, with exposure depending on application configuration. Attackers could exploit these flaws to inject malicious code, exhaust server resources, or steal sensitive data. Users are strongly advised to upgrade to Struts 7.4.0 (or 6.12.0 for the 6.x branch) to patch these critical weaknesses. Temporary workarounds like enforcing request-body limits or preformatting data can also mitigate risks until full patching is possible.
slides.hindiSummary: Apache Struts में चार नई कमजोरियां रिमोट कोड निष्पादन, सेवा से इनकार और डेटा प्रकटीकरण का कारण बन सकती हैं।
